calculators.title: Mortgage Payment Calculator
calculators.description: Calculate your monthly mortgage payment, view a full amortization schedule, and see how extra payments can save you thousands in interest. Free, private, no sign-up required.
calculators.ogDescription: Calculate your monthly mortgage payment, view a full amortization schedule, and see how extra payments can save you thousands in interest.
calculators.intro: Calculate your monthly mortgage payment instantly. See a full year-by-year amortization schedule, compare 15 vs 30 year terms, and discover how extra payments can save you thousands in interest — all in your browser, with no sign-up required.
howToUse: Enter the Home Price — the total purchase price of the property you are considering.
Enter your Down Payment — the amount you plan to pay upfront. A 20% down payment avoids PMI.
Set the Interest Rate — use your pre-approved rate or the current market average. As of 2026, rates range from 5.5% to 7%.
Choose the Loan Term — 30 years is most common. 15 years has higher payments but saves significantly on interest.
Add Extra Payments (optional) — even $100 extra per month can shave years off your loan.
Click Calculate — view your monthly payment, total interest, payoff date, and full amortization table.

example.scenario: Sarah and Mike are first-time homebuyers looking at a $400,000 home. They have saved $80,000 for a down payment (20%). Their lender offers a 6.5% interest rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage.
bullets: If they add $200 extra each month, they save ~$100,000 in interest and pay off the loan 6 years early.

benefits.title: Instant Results
benefits.desc: No waiting, no loading screens. Change any number and see results update in real time.

benefits.title: Full Amortization
benefits.desc: Year-by-year breakdown showing exactly how much goes to principal vs. interest.

benefits.title: Extra Payment Impact
benefits.desc: See how even small extra payments dramatically reduce your total interest.

benefits.title: 100% Private
benefits.desc: All calculations run in your browser. No data is ever sent to a server.

mistakes.title: Forgetting property taxes and insurance.
mistakes.desc: Your actual monthly payment will include property taxes, homeowners insurance, and possibly PMI — which can add $300–$600/month.

mistakes.title: Underestimating the down payment.
mistakes.desc: Putting down less than 20% triggers PMI, costing 0.5%–1% of the loan amount per year.

mistakes.title: Ignoring closing costs.
mistakes.desc: Closing costs run 2%–5% of the home price. On a $400,000 home, budget $8,000–$20,000.

faq.q: How do I calculate my monthly mortgage payment?
faq.a: Your monthly payment depends on the loan amount, interest rate, and loan term. Use the formula M = P [ r(1+r)^n ] / [ (1+r)^n − 1 ]. Or simply enter your numbers above.
An amortization schedule is a year-by-year breakdown of every payment. It shows how much goes to principal versus interest, and how your loan balance decreases over time.

faq.q: How much can I save with extra payments?
faq.a: On a $320,000 mortgage at 6.5% over 30 years, adding just $200/month saves approximately $100,000 in interest and pays off the loan about 6 years early.
